mechanisms.question: Why are orchestration and model routing separate decisions?
mechanisms.summary: Pi orchestration decides what work becomes a sub-agent task. The model router decides what capability tier should execute that task. Keeping those responsibilities separate prevents agent roles from becoming permanent model assignments.

why_sources.claim: routing is tier-based and independent from agent role

risks: If role names are mapped directly to concrete models, model choice becomes brittle as providers/models change.

mechanisms.question: Why does mundane interactive work bypass the three-tier complexity router?
mechanisms.summary: A mundane task can still require low latency. The three Pi tiers describe capability/complexity, so invocation context must distinguish synchronous interactive work from background work before routing mundane tasks to local hardware.

evidence.role: documents exactly three tiers: low, medium, high

why_sources.claim: the extension exposes three tiers, not a separate quick tier
latency sensitivity is independent from task complexity

uncertainties: Exact Pi extension point for feeding interactive/background metadata into the routing decision.
risks: If urgency is inferred only from prompt text, background work may be sent to hosted models or interactive work may feel unnecessarily slow.

mechanisms.question: How do low, medium, and high become local, economy, and premium execution?
mechanisms.summary: The three router tiers are treated as capability classes rather than fixed model identities: low maps to local Ollama, medium to a cost-efficient hosted model, and high to a frontier model.

evidence.lines: The three pi-model-router tiers map naturally to

evidence.role: profiles map low/medium/high to configurable models

why_sources.claim: profiles allow different concrete models per tier
keeping model names out of agent definitions makes the system easier to update

uncertainties: Exact local/economy/premium aliases should remain configurable and may change over time.
risks: A three-tier classifier can still misclassify tasks, so manual pin/override and debug visibility remain useful.

mechanisms.question: What does OpenRouter route if Pi already chose the model class?
mechanisms.summary: Pi chooses the model or model class. OpenRouter then serves hosted requests through its provider layer, handling provider selection and failover; optional model fallbacks are a second reliability layer.

evidence.role: documents separate model and provider routing plus failover

why_sources.claim: model selection and provider selection are separate decisions
provider failover is automatic and model fallback can be configured separately

risks: Letting both Pi and OpenRouter independently auto-select models would make routing harder to reason about and debug.

mechanisms.question: Why should workers ask for capabilities instead of named models?
mechanisms.summary: A worker's job describes the work, not the provider. Capability hints let the router choose an appropriate model while preserving reusable agent definitions.

why_sources.claim: do not hard-code concrete model names in reusable skills
model:auto can inherit the model registry

uncertainties: Whether Pi should encode these hints in task metadata, role metadata, or router rules.
risks: If hints are too vague, the router may need additional task metadata such as latency and privacy sensitivity.

mechanisms.question: How does an 18 GB M3 Pro change the local-agent policy?
mechanisms.summary: Local inference is treated as a cost/privacy/background resource, not as the default reasoning engine. Concurrency stays conservative and large local models are not required for correctness.

why_sources.claim: target hardware has 18 GB unified memory
one substantial local generation at a time avoids making memory contention part of normal routing

uncertainties: Benchmark the exact local model and context length on the target machine before fixing defaults.
risks: Aggressive local concurrency can cause memory pressure and make supposedly cheap background work slower than hosted alternatives.
